Supplementary modeled-hazard context

ASEAN flood-hazard screen

This audit screens public 30 m modeled coastal, fluvial, and pluvial depth scenarios against the same fixed ATLAS study boxes in Singapore, Jakarta, and Bangkok. It covers the present-day SSP5-8.5_2020 scenario at 10-, 100-, and 1,000-year return periods: 27 raster checks.

Interpretation boundary: these are modeled design conditions, not dated observed floods, event/baseline samples, or independent validation labels. Nodata and missing raster cells remain unknown and are excluded from wet-area estimates; they are never treated as dry.

Method

  • Use the registered 25 km × 25 km WGS84 bounding box for each city.
  • Transform the box to each raster’s UTM CRS and include pixels whose centers fall inside it.
  • Require single-band rasters at 30 m resolution; screen coastal, fluvial, and pluvial hazards at 10, 100, and 1,000 years.
  • Report valid-data coverage separately. Compute modeled wet area at depth >0 m and ≥0.10 m; this table shows the ≥0.10 m threshold.
  • Report counts over 30 m projected cells and only within valid-data cells. Source rasters and checksums are pinned in the JSON artifact.

Value integration and limits

The three-city screen adds comparable hazard-scenario context for major technology hubs. It can support descriptive prioritization alongside separately sourced asset, population, service-continuity, and equity information. It does not establish local customer demand, measured consequences, flood losses, or benefit. The broad study boxes and city-level model grids are not parcel exposure measurements.

  • Coverage is uneven: Jakarta fluvial valid coverage is 49.5%, and Bangkok fluvial coverage ranges from 29.2% to 31.0%.
  • Bangkok coastal modeled area is non-monotonic across return periods; verify scenario definitions before interpreting changes.
  • The source dataset README describes model validation, but its accompanying manuscript and validation register were not independently reviewed in this screening run.
  • This supplementary source covers only 3 of 16 registered areas; it does not meet all-area observational comparability or change confirmatory eligibility.

Source and reproducibility

Source: Open Multi-Hazard Flood Atlas, version 2; license: CC BY 4.0. Open the machine-readable audit JSON.

Reproduce with scripts/audit_asean_atlas_fixed_aoi.py and the three pinned archives. The audit fails closed on checksum, package metadata, CRS, resolution, or spatial-overlap mismatches. Canonical score remains 60/100 provisional and confirmatory eligibility remains 0/16.

ATLAS research prototype · Modeled hazard context only · No claim of independent validation
